citation: The Chicago Blue Book of Selected Names of Chicago and Suburban Towns, for the year ending 1894. Chicago: The Chicago Directory Company.
author: The Chicago Directory Company
describes_date: 1894 (the edition 'for the year ending 1894', canvassed from the September before)
locator: T-3266: the PRAIRIE AVENUE street-and-number list, numbers 1600-2140, and every line of the alphabetical list of names that gives a Prairie Avenue number in that range; each reading is a row of docs/RESEARCH/prairie-former-residents-3266/blue_book_prairie_readings.tsv.
rights_note: A United States publication of 1894; public domain.
access_notes: Read for T-3266 on 2026-10-30 from the item's OCR text (chicagobluebooko1894chic_djvu.txt) by docs/RESEARCH/prairie-former-residents-3266/read_blue_books.py. The OCR is not the page: a household is used only where the street list and the alphabetical list agree, or the alphabetical list prints it in two editions (tools/build_former_residents_1904.py).
note: A society register: it lists the households that received and were received, not every household, so a number it skips is silence, not vacancy. Used on the 1904 Prairie Avenue People cards for who lived in each house before (or, for a house nobody is listed in for 1904, after) the scene date.
what_it_supplies: which households the register listed at each Prairie Avenue number from 1600 to 2140 for 1894
what_it_does_not_supply: servants, young children, or households outside society
the date a household came or went within the year
the building's form, storeys, material or outline
